questions.enonce: How is the total capacity of two independent workstations placed in parallel calculated?
options: By taking the capacity of the slowest workstation.
By taking the average of both.
questions.explication: When two workstations performing the same operation are in parallel and independent (without risk of upstream shortage), their capacities are added together[span_0](start_span)[span_0](end_span).

questions.enonce: What determines the overall capacity of a production line composed of workstations in series without intermediate inventory?
options: The fastest workstation on the line.
The limiting workstation, i.e., the bottleneck.
The arithmetic mean of the capacities of all workstations.
The total number of operators assigned to the line.
questions.explication: The overall capacity of a production line is determined by the limiting capacity of the limiting workstation (the bottleneck)[span_1](start_span)[span_1](end_span).

questions.enonce: How is the projected workload calculated for a quantity Q of products passing through a line of n operations with times t_i?
options: Q multiplied by the sum of the operation times (Q × Σ t_i).
Q divided by the sum of the operation times.
Q plus the sum of the operation times.
questions.explication: The projected workload is equal to the quantity Q multiplied by the sum of all operation times, since each product must pass through all steps[span_2](start_span)[span_2](end_span).

questions.enonce: What range for the balancing measure (epsilon, ε) indicates that a production line is properly balanced?
questions.explication: A correct line balancing gives an epsilon (ε) measure between 0% and 5%[span_3](start_span)[span_3](end_span).
